notes_history.text: Admitted from ED with severe septic shock and peripheral mottling.

patients.progress_note_24h: ICU Day 1 Nursing Note: 72yo M admitted with severe septic shock secondary to community-acquired pneumonia. Refractory hypotension requiring escalating norepinephrine (0.24 mcg/kg/min) and vasopressin. Lactic acidosis worsening from 2.8 to 5.1 mmol/L. Intubated on volume-control with FiO2 70%, PEEP 14. Urine output < 15 mL/hr over past 5 hours despite aggressive crystalloid resuscitation. Emergent nephrology consultation placed for CRRT initiation. Guarded prognosis conveyed to family.

notes_history.author: Nurse Kelly Adams, RN
notes_history.text: Direct admit from ED. Arterial line placed in right radial artery. Severe peripheral hypoperfusion noted. Norepinephrine initiated at 0.10 mcg/kg/min.

notes_history.author: Dr. Sarah Chen, MD
notes_history.text:
S: Intubated, sedated on propofol/fentanyl.
O: MAP 58 on dual pressors. Lactate 5.1. Oliguric (<15 mL/hr).
A: Septic shock refractory with acute multiorgan failure.
P: Add vasopressin. Prepare right internal jugular line for emergent CRRT.

patients.attending_physician: Dr. Marcus Vance, MD (Surgical Critical Care)
patients.progress_note_24h: ICU Day 1 Progress Note: 58yo F admitted for routine hemodynamic monitoring following elective robotic sigmoid resection. Hemodynamically stable off all vasopressor support. Extubated in PACU; maintaining SpO2 98% on 2L nasal cannula. Surgical incisions clean and dry. Pain adequately controlled with IV acetaminophen and low-dose PCA. Adequate urine output > 45 mL/hr. Plan for morning transfer to surgical stepdown floor.

notes_history.author: Dr. Marcus Vance, MD
notes_history.text: Post-op arrival uneventful. EBL 75mL. Hemoglobin 11.8 stable. Flatus not yet passed. Clear liquids tolerated.

patients.progress_note_24h: CCU Nursing Assessment: 66yo M status post acute anterolateral STEMI with drug-eluting stent placement to proximal LAD. Initial transient hypotension stabilized on low-dose dopamine, successfully weaned off at hour 14. Serial troponins peaking. Bedside echo demonstrates moderate anterior hypokinesia, LVEF estimated 40-45%. Occasional PVCs noted on telemetry, no runs of VTach. Serum potassium repleted to 4.2. Hemodynamics stabilizing.

patients.diagnosis: Polytrauma, Bilateral Flail Chest & Severe ARDS
patients.progress_note_24h: ICU Progress Note: 79yo F with multitrauma including bilateral flail chest and pulmonary contusions following MVA. Developing acute severe ARDS with PaO2/FiO2 ratio 92. Refractory hypoxemia with SpO2 86-89% despite 100% FiO2 and neuromuscular blockade. Paralytics initiated. Neurological examination limited due to sedation. Oliguric with rising BUN and creatinine (2.4 mg/dL). Code status remains Full Code per surrogate decision maker.

ICU Day 1 Note: 63yo M admitted with severe acute gallstone pancreatitis. Large volume third-spacing with 6 liters crystalloid administered in 24 hours. Urine output recovering to 30-40 mL/hr. Persistent epigastric pain managed on hydromorphone. Afebrile. Serum lipase > 1200. Transferred to enteral feeding tube trial. Hemodynamics stable without pressors.

patients.diagnosis: Cardiogenic Shock post-CABG x4 with IABP Support
patients.progress_note_24h: CVICU Attending Note: 71yo M post emergent redo-CABG with low cardiac output syndrome. Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) 1:1 assist in place. Epinephrine 0.08 mcg/kg/min and milrinone 0.375 mcg/kg/min running. Cardiac index 1.8 L/min/m2. Mixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) 52%. Chest tube output 75 mL over past 4 hours. Renal function deteriorating.

NeuroICU Day 1: 44yo F status post successful endovascular coiling of anterior communicating artery aneurysm. Neurologically awake, alert, GCS 15. Following all commands. Strict SBP parameter < 140 mmHg maintained with nicardipine drip now weaned off. Denies focal deficits. Transcranial dopplers show no early vasospasm. EVD clamped.

patients.diagnosis: Severe Diabetic Ketoacidosis & E. Coli Urosepsis
patients.progress_note_24h: MICU Resident Assessment: 52yo M admitted with profound DKA (pH 7.08, bicarbonate 6, glucose 780 mg/dL) complicated by E. coli urosepsis. Aggressive insulin infusion and electrolyte replacement ongoing. Anion gap closed from 28 to 14 over 20 hours. Mentation improving, alert and oriented x3. IV fluids transitioned to D5 1/2NS + 20 mEq KCl. Urine output brisk (>70 mL/hr).
